title: Solver reconciliation: execution / evidence / workflow relevance
is_shadow: This is a pure read that REPORTS. It does not gate anything yet and persists nothing; the plan calls for the evaluator to stabilise before a runner preflight writes reconciliation events. It never rewrites solver_jobs.status and never appends an event.

three_questions.execution_state: RUNNING | TERMINAL_SUCCESS | TERMINAL_FAILURE | UNKNOWN. The job's own exit artifact settles it; without one a stale `running` row stays RUNNING because there is no per-job liveness signal, and a db-terminal row with no artifact is UNKNOWN rather than trusted.
three_questions.evidence_state: COMPLETE | INCOMPLETE | INVALID | NOT_REQUIRED, using the same two helpers and the same fail-closed shape as cli.solver_evidence_payload (receipt_ready=False, claim_limit=LEGACY_JOB_METADATA_ONLY) rather than a second notion of 'evidence complete'.
three_questions.workflow_relevance: REQUIRED | SUPERSEDED | ORPHANED | HISTORICAL | ADVISORY | UNRESOLVED.

proofs_implemented.SUPERSEDED: a later job (higher job_revision) in the same owner slot reached terminal success
proofs_implemented.HISTORICAL: the job is provably terminal and the project's committed cursor has passed the stage that owned it
proofs_implemented.ADVISORY: provably terminal and the cursor has completed its own stage

positive_proof_rule.why_cursor_counts_as_proof: project_state.last_completed_stage only advances through committed checkpoints, so it is evidence about the workflow rather than an inference about the job
positive_proof_rule.everything_else: UNRESOLVED - notably a job with no owner slot at all, which is the case where a guess would be most tempting and most wrong

design_fix_found_while_building: relevance first consulted the database's status claim, which made a stale `running` row report REQUIRED even though its exit artifact proved successful execution. Relevance now reads the reconciled execution state; the db claim is exposed only for diagnostics.
design_fix_performance: the first implementation called cli.solver_evidence_payload per job, which re-reads the whole event stream each time - quadratic on R (2484 events, 361 jobs) and it timed out. The event list is now read once.

interpretation.A: two ownerless jobs whose relevance cannot be proven -> UNRESOLVED, and they BLOCK. This is a genuine finding: A's completion rests on jobs the workflow cannot account for. The shadow evaluator reports it rather than inventing an answer.
interpretation.B: the residual stale `running` row is provably SUPERSEDED by a later success in the same owner slot -> no blocker.
interpretation.R: every job sits behind the committed cursor -> no blocker.

next_stage: G2 (A/B read-only anomalies + synthetic required/superseded/unresolved jobs), then S4.1
open_items: checkpoint receipts still do not bind job_id, which is why HISTORICAL needs the cursor as its proof; future receipts should bind the adopted completion receipt so UNRESOLVED narrows naturally
persisting the reconciliation is deliberately deferred until the evaluator is reviewed
